findings: The prefill is entirely kernel-bound. 2.013 s of kernel time against 1.991 s of measured prefill wall time is 101%, i.e. within noise of all of it, so there is no host-side or dispatch overhead to recover. This is why per-token cost is flat: it is the sum of a fixed per-layer kernel bill.

Matmuls are about 78% of the prefill - q5_1 staged grouped 35.5%, q8_0 dense tiled 28.1%, q4_k MMQ32 fused 9.4% and the single q5_k layer 5.5%. That confirms the flat per-token constant the length curve isolated is matmul cost, not attention and not launch overhead.

Layer 29 is visible as a single launch. gguf_q5_k_selected_grouped_row4_bf16_kernel is one call costing 110.89 ms, against 29 calls of the q5_1 kernel at 24.65 ms each. One layer is therefore about 4.5x a normal layer on the gate_up alone, before its q8_0 down, which is the campaign's second open item confirmed by kernel trace rather than estimated.

Attention is 15.0% at 512 tokens - 301.09 ms over 30 launches, about 10 ms per layer - and that is the baseline cost at a length where the length curve shows no penalty at all. This corrects the redirection in the previous entry: the curve measured only the growth past the window, and the tiled 512-wide-head kernel's headroom includes this flat 15%, not only the 12.6% that grows at 1024.

The MoE scheduler the campaign lists third is small on this platform - router logits 16.71 ms, group compact 13.04, gather 10.59 and router select 1.79, about 42 ms or 2.1% combined - rather than the 25 ms figure the campaign carries.
limits: One 512-token prefill, one box, one artifact, one profiling run. Timestamps rather than DurationNs, so overlapping streams would be double-counted; total matching wall to 1% indicates they are not.
Kernel time is not a promotion claim. This locates the next unit.
